title: Experience Definition
description:
An experience is an application: one or more pages with shared navigation, shared parameters, a drill-down graph and a single governance lifecycle. It is the unit of publication, promotion, approval and audit — pages are versioned as part of it, never independently, because a drill-down target that promotes separately from its source is a broken page waiting to happen.

The level above the page was missing from the original documentation set, yet every stated journey needs it: 'Security Overview' is a search page plus a detail page plus tabs plus drill-down, not a page.

kind.description: 'application' is a multi-page experience with navigation; 'single' is one page with no shell chrome, suitable for embedding; 'process' is workflow-hosted and reserved for v3.

workspaceId.description: Owning workspace — the sharing primitive and the unit against which governance weight is tiered.

pages.description: Pages keyed by id. Stored inline for small experiences and by reference for large ones; either way they version and promote together.

oneOf.description: Reference to a page stored separately, resolved at load. Used when an experience is large enough that transmitting every page for every render is wasteful.

parameters.description: Experience-scoped parameters shared by every page — as-of date, business unit, base currency. Declared once here rather than repeated per page, so a value chosen anywhere is carried consistently.

exposedInShell.description: Render a control for this parameter in the application shell, so it applies across pages.

dataSources.description: Experience-scoped data sources, for shell-level needs such as navigation badge counts and parameter value lists.

actions.description: Experience-scoped actions available from the shell.

environments.description: Environments this experience targets. The definition itself is environment-agnostic — a version promoted from UAT to production is byte-identical, and only the gateway's logical-to-physical binding differs. Listing environments here declares intent, not configuration.
